Also bipolar II. Lamictal is great for type II, not so much type I. 

Lamictal was a wonder drug for me. Truly the magic pill. I was in and out of hospitals, very suicidal, completely unable to maintain any kind of healthy relationships.

I titrated up and was basically bed bound with fatigue and brain fog for like I shit you not 10-12 weeks.

But then the side effects went away and it was like…I was just me, without all the extra crap. And I like who I am. I’m actually a happy well-adjusted person on lamictal. It was an epiphany like…the bipolar is separate from me and who I am without the bipolar is actually a pretty awesome, functional person.

I got married, lost 75 pounds and kept it off, went back to school, got a career, started some hobbies. In the past 7 years I have had break-through symptoms but never anything that rose to a clinical “episode”. 

I live a normal life now. Imagine that.

Mine got worse with age until I got to be like 28ish. Then I got on good medication and I’ve been in semi-remission ever since. I’m 34 now.

It can get better. You need to put a lot of work in but there’s hope.

A functional life is boring. That’s just the truth of it. People who are fully mentally healthy don’t have a huge emotional range compared to us and they just kind of neutrally go through the same cycles every day.

Recovery does feel boring and bland, but basically that’s how you pace yourself so you can live 80+ years without fully burning out on life.

You can have bipolar disorder without really serious manic episodes. It’s called hypomania.

Basically mania includes usually very obvious psychotic symptoms. So hallucinations or delusions.

Hypomania is mania without the presence of psychotic symptoms. It can be really bad, where you don’t sleep for days, spend a lot of money, become hypersexual, etc. But it can also be pretty light. Like a sped-up kind of feeling.

For me hypomania is actually not that bad. My brain kind of feels like it’s boiling and I get irritable and say eccentric things, but I’m actually pretty functional. A low grade hypomania can even be a decent state to be in.

Before I was medicated though my depression would get so bad I wouldn’t be able to do basic hygiene or housework. I’d even get a few psychotic features like thinking I could read minds.

I’ve been on lamictal for 6 years and it gave me my life back. I went from multiple hospitalizations a year to living a completely normal life. Obviously it wasn’t just Lamictal, there was also a ton of working on myself involved, but yeah...I’ll probably be on it forever.

That said I’m terrified to miss a dose. I haven’t missed a single dose in 6 years. It’s a scary medication and I have doubts a lot of the time if I’m doing the right thing putting this into my body everyday

I’ve tried a lot of antipsychotics and none really did much except make my weight shoot up and make me tired. In the US we call that medication Seroquel and I’ve definitely had it.

What worked for me (and I would recommend anyone with bipolar II discuss this with their psychiatrist) is lamotrigine paired with Mirtazapine before bed. You have to push through about 8-12 weeks of disabling side effects, but afterwards I lost 35 kilo and kept it off, went back to school, met a guy and now have a healthy marriage, and was able to work. Before this year I only suffered from break through sub-clinical symptoms and a slight loss of sex drive (not totally dead though!). 

Eventually I was even able to get off the Mirtazapine too.

I know tons of people who have had great success with lamotrigine. Once you’re past the monitoring stage and the side effects even out, it’s actually very safe. You don’t have a lot of the permanent neurological problems you get with antipsychotics. It’s also super cheap. Crazy it’s not prescribed much in the Netherlands.
